answers.M8-S1: The author already knows Mason-bees can find their nests from far away, and he does an experiment to show people that his bees really can do it.
answers.M8-S2: To show the trip was harder for the bees, because the wind made them fly low and slowed them down.
answers.M8-S3: They weren't in a big hurry. They stopped to collect food on the way, so the trip was easy for them.
answers.M8-S4: So Aglaé could tell which bees at the nest were the ones he carried away and not other bees.
answers.M8-S5: He was excited and sure the bees would come home, and at the end he is proven right when Aglaé shows the two bees arrived.
answers.M8-S6: It goes in time order, telling the steps of the experiment from catching the bees to the bees coming back.
answers.M8-S7: To show how fast the bees flew home even though they stopped for pollen, which proves they are really good at finding home.
answers.M8-S8: To show the experiment was hard and he made mistakes, so fewer bees could make it home.
answers.M8-S9: That the bees couldn't see landmarks, so they must have found their way home some other way, not by looking.
